q: What does a lender look at to judge if an MSME is ready for climate-linked finance?
title: Climate finance readiness for MSMEs
short: Clean records first: monthly energy and fuel data from bills, an emissions estimate that traces to those bills, a defined project with costed savings, and up-to-date compliance. Climate data supports the case; the credit decision still rests on cash flow.
audience: MSMEs preparing to approach banks or NBFCs for green or sustainability-linked loans

ul: 12 months of electricity and fuel bills.
An emissions figure that ties back to those bills.
Production data, so intensity per unit can be shown.
Quotes, a project report and expected energy savings.
How the savings will be measured after installation.
Who will report to the lender and how often.

p: Pollution control consents, GST filings and financial statements still decide most of the outcome. Gaps there matter more than a missing emissions figure.

senseible: Senseible turns invoices and bills into dated, fingerprinted emission records, the evidence a lender usually asks to see first.
